catalogue.install.title: Install the architect on your computer
catalogue.install.lead: On your machine, with your Confluence and your model: nothing goes through LEKA. Three steps, about ten minutes, no administrator rights.
catalogue.install.private: The package holds no secret. Download reserved to your organisation.
catalogue.install.step1Lead: Optional: you can also write them later, in the .env file.
catalogue.install.stay: They stay in this browser: LEKA never receives them. They are written into your installer, which deletes itself once used.
catalogue.install.urlHow.title: Where is the address?
catalogue.install.urlHow.steps.0: Open your Confluence in the browser.
catalogue.install.urlHow.steps.1: Copy the start of the address: up to « .atlassian.net » (Confluence Cloud), or your company server's address (Confluence Data Center).
catalogue.install.urlHow.steps.2: Confluence Data Center: leave the e-mail empty.
catalogue.install.tokenHow.title: Create my Confluence token
catalogue.install.tokenHow.steps.0: Confluence Cloud: open https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens (signed in with the same account).
catalogue.install.tokenHow.steps.1: Click « Create API token », name it « Architect », pick an expiry, then « Create ».
catalogue.install.tokenHow.steps.2: Click « Copy », then paste it in the Token field.
catalogue.install.tokenHow.steps.3: Confluence Data Center: your avatar top right → Profile → Personal access tokens → Create token.
catalogue.install.models.copilot: Copilot or Claude, in VS Code (no key)
catalogue.install.copilotSaid: Nothing to fill in: Copilot's model, or Claude's, thinks in VS Code. The installer sets everything up there.
catalogue.install.keyHow.title: Where is my key?
catalogue.install.keyHow.azure.0: Usually, your IT gives you these three details.
catalogue.install.keyHow.azure.1: Otherwise: https://portal.azure.com → your Azure OpenAI resource → « Keys and Endpoint »: copy « Key 1 » and the « Endpoint ».
catalogue.install.keyHow.azure.2: The deployment name: Azure AI Foundry → Deployments (e.g. gpt-4.1).
catalogue.install.keyHow.anthropic.1: « Create Key », name it, then copy it.
catalogue.install.keyHow.gemini.0: Open https://aistudio.google.com/apikey with your Google account.
catalogue.install.keyHow.gemini.1: « Create API key », then copy it.
catalogue.install.keyHow.mistral.1: « Create new key », then copy it.
catalogue.install.keyHow.openai.1: « Create new secret key », then copy it.
catalogue.install.keyHow.other.0: Any OpenAI-compatible API (an internal LLM, Ollama, vLLM…): its address (often ending in /v1), the model's name and its key, given by whoever hosts it.
catalogue.install.step2Lead: Both files land in your Downloads folder.
catalogue.install.filesHow.title: What is in these files?
catalogue.install.filesHow.steps.0: The agent (leka-architect-….zip): its code, its instructions, the drawing of the PowerPoint and the PDF. No secret.
catalogue.install.filesHow.steps.1: The installer (installer-architecte.sh, or .ps1 on Windows): the install commands and your details. Made by this browser, it deletes itself at the end of the install.
catalogue.install.step3Lead: Open the {terminal}, paste this command, then Enter: 2 to 3 minutes.
catalogue.install.openHow.title: Open the {terminal}
catalogue.install.openHow.windows.0: Press the Windows key, type « PowerShell », then Enter. No administrator rights needed.
catalogue.install.openHow.windows.1: Right-click in the window to paste the command, then Enter.
catalogue.install.openHow.macos.0: Press Cmd + Space, type « Terminal », then Enter.
catalogue.install.openHow.macos.1: Cmd + V to paste the command, then Enter.
catalogue.install.openHow.macos.2: If macOS asks for access to the Downloads folder: « OK ».
catalogue.install.openHow.linux.0: Ctrl + Alt + T, or look for « Terminal » in your applications.
catalogue.install.openHow.linux.1: Ctrl + Shift + V to paste the command, then Enter.
catalogue.install.does.0: It checks Python (3.10 or later); otherwise it says where to get it.
catalogue.install.does.1: It unzips the agent into the « architecte » folder of your account and installs it.
catalogue.install.does.2: It writes your details into architecte/.env and sets up Copilot in VS Code.
catalogue.install.does.3: It creates the « Lancer l'architecte » button, checks it reads your Confluence spaces, then opens the folder.
catalogue.install.launch: To launch: double-click « Lancer l'architecte » in the architecte folder. It lists your spaces, asks for the space, the journey and the perimeter, then opens the PowerPoint and the PDF (3 to 5 minutes).
catalogue.install.copilotHow.title: With Copilot in VS Code
catalogue.install.copilotHow.steps.0: Open VS Code → File → Open Folder… → pick « architecte », in your home folder.
catalogue.install.copilotHow.steps.1: If VS Code asks to trust the folder, or to start the « leka-architect » MCP server: accept.
catalogue.install.copilotHow.steps.2: Open Copilot's chat and pick the « Agent » mode.
catalogue.install.copilotHow.steps.3: Type: /architecte-applicatif Construis l'architecture du parcours Paiement CB sur le périmètre Digital
catalogue.install.copilotHow.steps.4: Copilot reads your Confluence with the architect's tools, then writes the PowerPoint and the PDF into the rapport-architecture folder.
catalogue.install.laterHow.title: Change my details later
catalogue.install.laterHow.steps.0: Open the .env file of the architecte folder (TextEdit, Notepad…).
catalogue.install.laterHow.steps.2: The ARCHITECT_LLM_… lines: the model. Delete them to think with Copilot.
catalogue.install.laterHow.steps.3: Save: the next launch uses them.
catalogue.install.manualHow.title: If your computer refuses scripts: by hand
catalogue.install.manualHow.lead: Copy these blocks into the {terminal}, one after the other.
catalogue.install.manualEnv: In the .env file that opens: your details, then save
catalogue.install.manualCheck: Check: your spaces are listed, their key on the left
catalogue.install.manualRun: Launch: replace MO with your space's key, then the journey and the perimeter
catalogue.install.problemsHow.title: An error message?
catalogue.install.problemsHow.steps.0: « Il faut Python 3.10 ou plus »: install it (the link is in the message), then run the same command again.
catalogue.install.problemsHow.steps.1: « L'agent n'est pas dans Téléchargements »: first click « Download the agent ».
catalogue.install.problemsHow.steps.2: « L'installation a échoué »: Internet is needed; behind a company proxy, see your IT.
catalogue.install.problemsHow.steps.3: « Le token Confluence est vide », or refused: check the token in architecte/.env.
catalogue.install.problemsHow.steps.4: « L'espace … est introuvable »: take a key shown on the left of the spaces list.

catalogue.summaries.standing: The state of what the request is about: its lifecycle, what LEKA knows of it, what it already concluded.

catalogue.summaries.documentation: What describes it, and whether that is current.
catalogue.summaries.compliance: What a thing of its kind should have, checked.
catalogue.summaries.migration: Where it moves to, what relies on it, what it relies on.
catalogue.summaries.action: An action asked on systems: what it reaches, its constraints, the last deployment.
catalogue.summaries.synthesis: The analysis answered in words: each point cites what it rests on.
catalogue.summaries.evolution: What LEKA learned in the period: what appeared, changed or went.
catalogue.summaries.architecture-dossier: A journey's full architecture dossier: standing, dependencies, documentation, then the architect's deck.
catalogue.summaries.incident-review: An incident reviewed end to end: what happened and why, what changed before, who owns it.
catalogue.summaries.release-readiness: Whether a service is ready for its next release: how it ships, its recent incidents, how far a failure would reach.
catalogue.summaries.application-architec: Generates your application architecture documentation, structured as ArchiMate, from your Confluence.
catalogue.summaries.architecture-analysi: An application's architecture explained: its parts, its dependencies, its weak points.
catalogue.summaries.detect-undocumented-: Dependencies seen in production or in code that no documentation describes.
catalogue.summaries.map-service-ownershi: A service's real owner, from commits and tickets.
catalogue.summaries.correlate-deploy-wit: Ties a rise in latency or errors to the deployment that may explain it.
catalogue.summaries.incident-investigati: An incident's timeline, what it reached, its likely cause, and its post-mortem drafted.
catalogue.summaries.infrastructure-analy: Where a service runs, on which resources, what is shared, what is a single point of failure.
catalogue.summaries.data-analysis: Where data lives, who reads or writes it, who owns it, where it flows.
catalogue.summaries.documentation-assist: How well something is documented, and a first draft of its documentation, nothing invented.
catalogue.summaries.security-review: What exposes an application: its sensitive data, what reaches it, what to check first.
catalogue.summaries.test-analysis: What to test before or after a change: what it touches, what depends on it, what broke.
catalogue.summaries.code-review: A pull request reviewed: what it touches, what it risks, who should look at it.
catalogue.summaries.release-analysis: A release analysed: what went out, what it touched, what followed, the next one's risk.
catalogue.summaries.code-change: Changes a repository's code: a diff proposed, reviewed by a person, then the pull request.
catalogue.summaries.build-fixer: Why a build breaks, and a fix proposed: never applied without you.
catalogue.summaries.debug-assistant: A misbehaving service's likely causes, ranked: what changed, what it depends on.
catalogue.summaries.ui-quality-review: Whether an application's screens are finished: loading, empty, error, on a phone, with long text.
catalogue.summaries.accessibility-audit: An application's accessibility to the keyboard, screen readers and in contrast: against WCAG 2.2 and the RGAA.
catalogue.summaries.design-review: The interface reviewed as a design engineer would: design system, animations, phone, real-world data; before, after, why.
catalogue.summaries.motion-review: An application's animations: useful or not, their timing, reduced motion respected, their smoothness.
catalogue.summaries.codebase-explorer: Finding your way in a repository's code: how it is organised, where a feature lives, how to build, run and test it.
catalogue.summaries.test-generation: The missing tests, written by LEKA: a diff a person reviews, then the pull request.
catalogue.summaries.qa-acceptance: A pull request accepted or not: each expected criterion, its status and its proof (the code, the test, the CI).
catalogue.summaries.api-design-review: An API reviewed: what a change breaks for those calling it, and its consistency (errors, pagination, what it exposes).
catalogue.summaries.reliability-analysis: What makes a service fragile: its points of failure, what happens when a dependency falls, the failures that hide, the incidents that recur.
catalogue.summaries.dependency-analysis: Your code's third-party packages: their known vulnerabilities, which matter, the version that fixes them, what runs at install time.
catalogue.summaries.database-review: A database reviewed: its schema's integrity, the indexes its queries need, the migrations that would lock or lose data.
catalogue.summaries.performance-analysis: Where a slow request's time goes, what will not hold as the data grows, and what to measure to prove it.
catalogue.summaries.migration-planning: The plan to migrate without breaking: what is touched and who depends on it, reversible steps in the right order, the switch and the retirement.
catalogue.summaries.regression-analysis: What a change could break that used to work: the behaviours it alters, what depends on them, the tests guarding them.
catalogue.summaries.change-impact-analys: How far a change reaches: the services, data, teams and processes it touches, and who must know.

outcome.expectedBody: What should be true once the actions ran. LEKA then verifies it in your company's model, and with the system that acted.

outcome.settle: First read on {at}, once the action has settled.

sources.custom.title: How does LEKA reach your tool?
sources.custom.intro: For a tool LEKA does not know yet: you describe its API, and LEKA treats it as a native source (test, scope, sync, health, history).
sources.custom.methods.custom_rest.title: REST API
sources.custom.methods.custom_rest.body: Your tool answers in JSON at https addresses. LEKA reads them, page after page, at every sync.
sources.custom.methods.custom_rest.needs: the API's address, a token or a key, and the resources to read
sources.custom.methods.custom_graphql.bo: Your tool exposes a GraphQL endpoint. LEKA sends your queries, read-only, and follows the cursors.
sources.custom.methods.custom_graphql.ne: the endpoint, a token, and one query per resource
sources.custom.methods.custom_webhook.bo: Your tool sends its changes as they happen. LEKA receives them at an address of the source's own, calling nothing.
sources.custom.methods.custom_webhook.ne: a shared secret, and what each event holds
sources.custom.unsupported.0: Signing in through a browser (OAuth, SSO, SAML): an API token or key is needed.
sources.custom.unsupported.1: Answers other than JSON: XML, SOAP, CSV, files.
sources.custom.unsupported.2: A tool on your internal network, over http or at a private address: LEKA only reaches public https addresses.
sources.custom.unsupported.3: Self-signed certificates or ones from an internal authority, and client certificates (mutual TLS).
sources.custom.unsupported.4: Windows (Kerberos, NTLM) or Digest authentication, and signed requests (AWS SigV4).
sources.custom.unsupported.5: Writing to your tool: LEKA only reads.
sources.custom.unsupportedContact: Does your tool need one of them? Write to support@leka-core.com: that is what decides what comes next. And if the test meets one, it says so.

sources.fields.organization.label: Organisation
sources.fields.organization.help: Empty: the repositories the token's owner sees.
sources.fields.group.label: Group
sources.fields.group.help: “acme” or “acme/platform”, subgroups included. Empty: the projects the token's owner is a member of.
sources.fields.workspace.label: Workspace
sources.fields.base_url.label: API address
sources.fields.base_url.help: Change only for an instance you host.
sources.fields.token.label: Access token
sources.fields.token.help: A read-only token is enough. It is encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fields.email.label: Account email
sources.fields.email.help: Only for an Atlassian API token.
sources.fields.access_key_id.label: Access key ID
sources.fields.access_key_id.help: The key of an IAM user with a read-only policy (see the documentation).
sources.fields.secret_access_key.label: Secret access key
sources.fields.role_arn.label: Role to assume
sources.fields.role_arn.help: Recommended: a read-only role in the account that the key assumes. Empty: the key reads itself.
sources.fields.external_id.label: External ID
sources.fields.external_id.help: The one the role's trust policy requires.
sources.fields.tenant_id.label: Tenant ID
sources.fields.tenant_id.help: The Microsoft Entra tenant id of the service principal.
sources.fields.client_id.label: Application (client) ID
sources.fields.client_id.help: The service principal's, with the Reader role on the subscriptions to read.
sources.fields.client_secret.label: Client secret
sources.fields.service_account_key.label: Service account key
sources.fields.service_account_key.help: The JSON file downloaded from Google Cloud, whole. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fields.site.label: Atlassian site
sources.fields.api_key.label: API key
sources.fieldsOf.github.pull_requests.he: LEKA opens a pull request (a new branch, one commit, never a merge) for a code change a person accepted. The token needs Contents and Pull requests in write.
sources.fieldsOf.splunk.base_url.label: Splunk API address
sources.fieldsOf.splunk.base_url.help: On the management port: https://acme.splunkcloud.com:8089, or your own Splunk's, https, with a recognised certificate, reachable from the internet.
sources.fieldsOf.splunk.token.label: Authentication token
sources.fieldsOf.splunk.token.help: Settings → Tokens, for a user whose role sees the apps to read. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.kibana.base_url.label: Kibana address
sources.fieldsOf.kibana.base_url.help: https://acme.kb.europe-west1.gcp.cloud.es.io, or your own Kibana's: https, reachable from the internet.
sources.fieldsOf.kibana.api_key.label: Elastic API key
sources.fieldsOf.kibana.api_key.help: Its encoded form (Stack Management → API keys), with read access to alert rules, cases and dashboards. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.grafana.base_url.label: Grafana address
sources.fieldsOf.grafana.base_url.help: https://acme.grafana.net, or your own Grafana's: https, reachable from the internet.
sources.fieldsOf.grafana.token.label: Service account token
sources.fieldsOf.grafana.token.help: glsa_…, a service account's with the Viewer role (Administration → Service accounts). Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.pagerduty.api_key.label: API key
sources.fieldsOf.pagerduty.api_key.help: A read-only REST API key (Integrations → API Access Keys, “Read-only” ticked). Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.pagerduty.region.label: Region
sources.fieldsOf.pagerduty.region.help: us, or eu if your PagerDuty account is hosted in Europe.
sources.fieldsOf.datadog.site.label: Datadog site
sources.fieldsOf.datadog.site.help: Your organisation's: datadoghq.com, datadoghq.eu, us3.datadoghq.com… You may paste your Datadog's address.
sources.fieldsOf.datadog.logs_query.help: Which logs to read, in Datadog's search syntax. By default, the errors: status:error.
sources.fieldsOf.datadog.application_key: A service account's, with the Datadog Read Only role, scoped to monitors_read, events_read, incident_read, metrics_read, logs_read_data and apm_service_catalog_read. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.datadog.api_key.label: API key
sources.fieldsOf.datadog.api_key.help: An API key of the organisation (Organization Settings → API Keys). Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.jira.token.label: API token
sources.fieldsOf.jira.token.help: An Atlassian token cannot be limited to reading: create it on a dedicated account, with no admin rights, that sees only what LEKA should read. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.jira.issues.label: Create the accepted tickets
sources.fieldsOf.jira.issues.help: LEKA creates in Jira the tickets a person accepted in a deliverable: new issues, in the projects this source reads, never an edit. The account must be able to create issues in those projects.
sources.fieldsOf.confluence.token.label: API token
sources.fieldsOf.confluence.token.help: An Atlassian token cannot be limited to reading: create it on a dedicated account, with no admin rights, that sees only what LEKA should read. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.confluence.pages.label: Publish the accepted pages
sources.fieldsOf.confluence.pages.help: LEKA publishes in Confluence the pages a person accepted in a deliverable: new pages, in the spaces this source reads, never an edit. The account must be able to add pages in those spaces.
sources.fieldsOf.linear.api_key.label: API key
sources.fieldsOf.linear.api_key.help: A personal key (lin_api_…). It is encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.asana.token.label: Personal access token
sources.fieldsOf.asana.token.help: A dedicated member's, not an admin's: My settings → Apps → Developer apps. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.trello.token.label: Token
sources.fieldsOf.trello.token.help: Authorised read-only (scope=read) by the key's owner. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.trello.api_key.label: API key
sources.fieldsOf.trello.api_key.help: A Power-Up's, from trello.com/power-ups/admin. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.clickup.token.label: Personal token
sources.fieldsOf.clickup.token.help: pk_…, a dedicated member's: Settings → Apps → API Token. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.monday.token.label: API token
sources.fieldsOf.monday.token.help: A dedicated member's, not an admin's: avatar → Developers → API token. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.slab.token.label: API token
sources.fieldsOf.slab.token.help: The workspace's, from Team settings → Developer (Business and Enterprise plans). It reads as the Slab Bot. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.guru.token.label: API token
sources.fieldsOf.guru.token.help: Preferably a collection token, read-only; else a dedicated user's. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.guru.username.label: Username
sources.fieldsOf.guru.username.help: For a collection token: the collection's id. For a user token: the user's email.
sources.fieldsOf.google_workspace.servic: The JSON file downloaded from Google Cloud, whole, from a project with the Google Drive API on. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.google_workspace.subjec: The account, dedicated and read-only, the service account acts as: by domain-wide delegation, with the drive.readonly scope. Empty: the service account itself, which sees only what is shared with its address.
sources.fieldsOf.microsoft_365.tenant_id: The Microsoft Entra tenant id of the application.
sources.fieldsOf.microsoft_365.client_id: The application's, with Microsoft Graph's application permissions Sites.Read.All, Files.Read.All and User.Read.All, consented by an admin.
sources.fieldsOf.postgresql.host.label: Host
sources.fieldsOf.postgresql.host.help: The server's name or public address, reachable from the internet: db.acme.com. A private address is refused.
sources.fieldsOf.postgresql.port.label: Port
sources.fieldsOf.postgresql.database.hel: The database to describe. LEKA reads its catalogue (schemas, tables, columns, keys), never its rows.
sources.fieldsOf.postgresql.username.hel: A dedicated role, with CONNECT on the database and USAGE on the schemas to describe. No SELECT is needed.
sources.fieldsOf.postgresql.password.hel: The role's. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.mysql.host.label: Host
sources.fieldsOf.mysql.host.help: The server's name or public address, reachable from the internet: db.acme.com. A private address is refused.
sources.fieldsOf.mysql.port.label: Port
sources.fieldsOf.mysql.username.label: Account
sources.fieldsOf.mysql.username.help: A dedicated account, with only the REFERENCES privilege on the databases to describe: it shows their structure, not their rows.
sources.fieldsOf.mysql.password.label: Password
sources.fieldsOf.mysql.password.help: The account's. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.mariadb.host.label: Host
sources.fieldsOf.mariadb.host.help: The server's name or public address, reachable from the internet: db.acme.com. A private address is refused. The server must accept TLS: it does by default since MariaDB 11.4, and on Amazon RDS.
sources.fieldsOf.mariadb.port.label: Port
sources.fieldsOf.mariadb.username.label: Account
sources.fieldsOf.mariadb.username.help: A dedicated account, with only the REFERENCES privilege on the databases to describe: it shows their structure, not their rows.
sources.fieldsOf.mariadb.password.label: Password
sources.fieldsOf.mariadb.password.help: The account's. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.sqlserver.host.label: Host
sources.fieldsOf.sqlserver.host.help: The server's name or public address, reachable from the internet: db.acme.com. A private address is refused. A named instance is reached by its port, not host\instance.
sources.fieldsOf.sqlserver.port.label: Port
sources.fieldsOf.sqlserver.database.help: The database to describe. LEKA reads its catalogue (schemas, tables, columns, keys), never its rows.
sources.fieldsOf.sqlserver.username.help: A dedicated SQL login, with a user in the database and VIEW DEFINITION on the schemas to describe. No SELECT is needed.
sources.fieldsOf.sqlserver.password.help: The login's. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.oracle.host.label: Host
sources.fieldsOf.oracle.host.help: The server's name or public address, reachable from the internet: db.acme.com. A private address is refused.
sources.fieldsOf.oracle.port.label: TLS port
sources.fieldsOf.oracle.port.help: TCPS's: usually 2484, 1522 on Autonomous Database. LEKA requires TLS; Oracle's native encryption is not enough.
sources.fieldsOf.oracle.service_name.hel: The database's service: ORCLPDB1, or that of the pluggable database to describe.
sources.fieldsOf.oracle.username.label: User
sources.fieldsOf.oracle.username.help: A dedicated user, with CREATE SESSION and REFERENCES on each table and view to describe. No SELECT is needed.
sources.fieldsOf.oracle.password.label: Password
sources.fieldsOf.oracle.password.help: The user's. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.custom_graphql.endpoint: The GraphQL API's address, https and public: https://api.acme.com/graphql.
sources.fieldsOf.custom_graphql.auth.hel: How LEKA sends the secret to the API.
sources.fieldsOf.custom_graphql.auth_nam: For a key in a header (X-API-Key) or in the URL (api_key): its name.
sources.fieldsOf.custom_graphql.definiti: For each resource, its GraphQL query (read-only), where its items are in the answer, its pagination and what each field means, as JSON. The shortest: {"resources": [{"name": "issues", "query": "query { issues { id title } }", "items": "data.issues", "mapping": {"id": "id", "title": "title"}}]}
sources.fieldsOf.custom_graphql.secret.h: The token, the API key or the password. Encrypted, and never shown again. Empty without authentication.
sources.fieldsOf.custom_graphql.username: For a user and password authentication.
sources.fieldsOf.custom_webhook.signatur: How the system signs what it sends, with the secret. HMAC-SHA256: GitHub, Shopify, most in-house tools. Standard Webhooks: systems that follow standardwebhooks.com. Token: GitLab.
For HMAC-SHA256 and the token: the header that carries it (X-Hub-Signature-256 for GitHub). Empty: X-Leka-Signature, or X-Leka-Token.
sources.fieldsOf.custom_webhook.definiti: What a delivery may be, as JSON: for each resource, the condition that recognises it, where its items are, what each field means, and what says they were deleted. The shortest: {"resources": [{"name": "tickets", "items": "ticket", "mapping": {"id": "id", "title": "subject"}}]}
sources.fieldsOf.custom_webhook.secret.h: The same on both sides, 16 characters at least: for Standard Webhooks, the whsec_… the system gives. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.custom_rest.base_url.he: The base address, https and public: https://api.acme.com/v2. Each resource's path is added to it.
sources.fieldsOf.custom_rest.auth.label: Authentication
sources.fieldsOf.custom_rest.auth.help: How LEKA sends the secret to the API.
sources.fieldsOf.custom_rest.auth_name.h: For a key in a header (X-API-Key) or in the URL (api_key): its name.
The resources to read, their pagination and what each field means, as JSON. The shortest: {"resources": [{"name": "tickets", "path": "/tickets", "items": "data", "mapping": {"id": "id", "title": "subject"}}]}
sources.fieldsOf.custom_rest.secret.help: The token, the API key or the password. Encrypted, and never shown again. Empty without authentication.
sources.fieldsOf.custom_rest.username.he: For a user and password authentication.
sources.fieldsOf.supabase.host.label: Pooler host
sources.fieldsOf.supabase.host.help: The project's Session pooler (Connect, in Supabase): aws-0-<region>.pooler.supabase.com. The direct host, db.<project>.supabase.co, has an IPv6 address only.
sources.fieldsOf.supabase.port.label: Port
sources.fieldsOf.supabase.database.label: Database
sources.fieldsOf.supabase.username.label: Role
sources.fieldsOf.supabase.username.help: A dedicated role, created in the SQL editor, followed by the project's id: leka_reader.<project>. It needs USAGE on the schemas to describe, no SELECT.
sources.fieldsOf.supabase.password.label: Password
sources.fieldsOf.supabase.password.help: The role's. Encrypted, and never shown again.
sources.fieldsOf.mongodb.address.label: Address
sources.fieldsOf.mongodb.address.help: The one MongoDB gives, without user or password: mongodb+srv://cluster0.abcd.mongodb.net for Atlas, mongodb://db.acme.com:27017 otherwise. Reachable from the internet.
sources.fieldsOf.mongodb.auth_database.h: Where the account is defined: admin, on Atlas and most servers.
sources.fieldsOf.mongodb.username.label: Account
sources.fieldsOf.mongodb.username.help: A dedicated account, with a role limited to listCollections, listIndexes, collStats and dbStats on the databases to describe: it sees their structure, never a document.
sources.fieldsOf.mongodb.password.label: Password
sources.fieldsOf.mongodb.password.help: The account's. Encrypted, and never shown again.
